lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: email and message structure

objective: Learners draft one real professional-style email using a four-part structure, a clear subject line, a specific greeting, a body with exactly one request stated plainly, and a closing with a name, addressed to a real fictional scenario such as asking a coach about a schedule conflict or a teacher about a missed assignment.
scenario: The learner picks one realistic scenario they might genuinely face, such as asking a coach, teacher, or activity leader a real question, and drafts a complete email following the four-part structure, without sending it to anyone since no real account or recipient is used in this task.
safetyNotes: This draft is never sent as part of the lesson; no real email account or recipient address is required.
materials: the four-part structure template on this task sheet

tasks.directions: Pick one realistic scenario where you would genuinely need to email an adult outside your family.

prompts.text: Describe the scenario and the one specific thing you need from the recipient.

tasks.directions: Draft your email using all four parts: a specific subject line, a greeting, a body with exactly one clearly stated request, and a closing with your name.

prompts.text: My subject line describes the specific topic, not a vague word like 'Question.'
My body states exactly one request in plain, direct language.
My closing includes my name and, if relevant, one identifying detail the recipient would need (such as which class or team).

tasks.directions: Read your draft out loud once, then revise it if any sentence would confuse the recipient about what you are asking.

prompts.text: Name one sentence you changed after reading it aloud, and explain why the original version could have confused the recipient.
Explain one specific choice you made about tone or wording because you were writing to an adult outside your family rather than to a friend.

remediation: If a learner's email buries the request inside multiple unrelated sentences, reteach by having them state the request first as a single bare sentence with no context, then build the rest of the email's structure around that one clear sentence.
extension: Have the learner draft a second email for a different realistic scenario that requires declining a request rather than making one, using the same four-part structure.
